pitch: Factory's Droids are AI agents that take on real software engineering work, from migrations and refactors to code review, testing, and incident response.

useCases.name: Migrations and modernization
useCases.pain: Legacy code and framework upgrades eat months of senior engineering time.
useCases.value: Droids can take on large migrations and refactors in parallel, so the team modernizes without pausing roadmap work.
useCases.question: Which migration or upgrade is on the roadmap that nobody has had time to start?
useCases.metric: Share of the migration completed by Droids during the pilot

useCases.name: Developer velocity
useCases.pain: Hiring can't keep pace with the roadmap, and engineers lose time to toil instead of features.
useCases.value: Droids can pick up tickets end to end, so the same team ships more of the roadmap.
useCases.question: How big is the backlog compared to what the team ships each quarter?
useCases.metric: Tickets completed per sprint, before and during the pilot

useCases.name: Code review and quality
useCases.pain: Code reviews slow down merges, and test coverage lags behind new code.
useCases.value: Droids can review pull requests and write tests, so quality improves without slowing merges.
useCases.question: How long does a typical pull request wait for review?
useCases.metric: Time to first review and change in test coverage

useCases.name: Engineering efficiency
useCases.pain: Budgets are flat or shrinking while delivery expectations stay the same.
useCases.value: Droids can help a leaner team keep shipping, with clear visibility into the work completed.
useCases.question: What has leadership asked engineering to deliver with the current headcount?
useCases.metric: Engineering hours saved on the pilot's target work

useCases.name: Secure, governed AI adoption
useCases.pain: Engineers want AI tools, but security and compliance teams need control over code and data.
useCases.value: Factory gives engineering leaders a governed way to adopt AI agents, so adoption happens with security's approval instead of through unapproved tools.
useCases.question: What does your security team require before approving an AI coding tool?
useCases.metric: Security review approved, with the controls the customer requires

personas.why: Must approve any AI tool that touches source code.
Owns the engineering budget and roadmap commitments.

personas.titles: Staff or Principal Engineer, Engineering Manager
personas.why: Tests Droids on real code and shapes the team's opinion.

personas.titles: Director of Engineering, Head of Platform or Developer Experience
personas.why: Feels the day-to-day pain and can sponsor a pilot.

discoveryQuestions: How does your team use AI coding tools today, if at all?
Who would need to approve a pilot, and what would make it a success?
